title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as far as pages 91–93 show. The 'Analysis situs' axiomatics works with a set M of 'multiplicités'. They behave like closed cells or strata of a tame (moderately stratified) space. M carries:
- an order ≤;
- a relation ≪, roughly 'is contained in / lies in the closure-boundary of';
- the relation ≱;
- for each X a boundary ∂X and an 'interior' X°, a set of elements Z with Z ≪ X but Z not ≪ ∂X (page 91 has X° ⊂ Ouv(X)).

There is also Σ_M, the ordered set of 'supports' (parties-supports) for M. It has Sups and a canonical complement anti-involution C_M (page 93). It plays the role of the lattice of constructible or definable subsets of the underlying space.

Page 91 proves a criterion for Y ∈ X°. It then starts proving that two incomparable, distinct elements X, Y have disjoint interiors; this is later strengthened to X° ∥ Y° (cf. p. 95). It then considers a subset Φ ⊂ M of mutually compatible multiplicités and notes Φ = F̃, the image of a family F (a dissection indexed by an ordered set I).

Page 92 opens with a structural remark: the situation now depends on I only through the structures (M, ≤, ≪, ≱). A crossed-out passage abandons an idea of introducing a separate dissection or ordered set.

The main definition: for each finite part A of F̃ = Φ, set
S_A = Supp_M(⋃_{X∈A} X°) = Sup_{Σ_M, X∈A} Supp(X°) ∈ Σ_M.
The second equality expresses that Supp commutes with unions. Under a supplementary axiom ('Ax. suppl. 1'), Supp X° = X°: each open interior is already a support.

By associativity of Sups, A = ⋃ A_i gives S_A = Sup_{Σ_M} S_{A_i}. This yields an increasing map P(F̃) → Σ_M, A ↦ S_A, which preserves (finite) joins.

Purpose (page 93): Grothendieck wants to show that this map is an order-isomorphism of a sub-poset of P(F̃) onto a sub-poset of Σ_M. He also wants it to commute with arbitrary Sups and Infs, to satisfy S_{A∖B} = S_A ∩ C_M(S_B) for B ⊂ A, and to send closed parts of F̃ to the supports they generate.

In modern terms: the open cells of a decomposition, being pairwise disjoint, generate a complete Boolean subalgebra of the lattice of supports. That subalgebra is isomorphic to the power set of the set of cells. This is the standard 'atoms of a cell decomposition' picture, here derived from purely order-theoretic axioms.
errors: The definition is stated for finite parts A of F̃, but the map is then asserted on all of P(F̃). Either F̃ is tacitly finite, or Sups of arbitrary families in Σ_M are needed. Page 93 indeed asks for arbitrary (transfinite) Sups.
The equality Supp(⋃ X°) = Sup Supp(X°) is used without comment. It requires Supp to commute with (finite) unions, which is presumably an axiom or earlier lemma not visible here.
Monotonicity and join-preservation are routine. Injectivity and Inf-preservation (page 93) are not proved here and depend on the disjointness X° ∥ Y° established on pages 91/95.

ideas.what: Assigning to each set of compatible cells the support generated by the union of their interiors, giving a join-preserving increasing map from the power set of the cells to the lattice of supports.
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra generated by the cells of a cell/stratification decomposition (atoms of the algebra of definable/constructible sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in o-minimal/tame topology (cell decomposition: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s) and in stratification theory
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5–6); this axiomatic development is unpublished

ideas.what: Remark that the construction depends on the indexing ordered set I only through the order-theoretic structures (M, ≤, ≪, ≱).
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic/combinatorial (poset-theoretic) description of a stratified space, cf. face posets and exit-path/stratification posets

ideas.what: Supplementary axiom ensuring that interiors X° are themselves supports.
ideas.modern_name: Axiom that open strata are constructible/definable (frontier condition-type axiom)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratification theory (Whitney/Thom/Mather frontier conditions)

missed.claim: This page belongs to an unpublished, purely order-theoretic axiomatization of tame topology (multiplicités, supports Σ_M with complement anti-involution, relations ≪ and ∂). Its goal is to show that a decomposition into compatible cells yields a complete Boolean sub-algebra of supports. The content of this page is routine, but the axiomatic framework as a whole was never published or developed by others.
missed.quote: On a ainsi une application P(F̃) ⟶ Σ_M, A ↦ S_A ... application évidemment croissante.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible lattice-theoretic foundation for tame topology alternative to o-minimality. The page itself adds only a routine step.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine definitional step (join-preserving map from subsets of cells to supports) inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. No new result appears on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: 'A1 suppl. 1' is more likely 'Ax. suppl. 1' (axiome supplémentaire 1).

'disclosjoint[?]' at the start: the first word is illegible; it may be 'situation' or similar ('... actuelle ne dépendant de I que par l'intermédiaire des structures M, ≤, ≪, ≱'). 'Structures' rather than 'Strates' is plausible.
Subscripts 'x∈A' in the image read 'X∈A' (or are carelessly written lowercase); the summand is X°.
The last line reads '·application évidemment croissante.' and the text before the displayed formula reads 'On a ainsi une application'.
